answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Work waits on the gale until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the trellis of the next round. Written in a verbs first, step by step register, it stays short. The design leans on time-locked work history, published publicly on failure, idle agents bleed standing. What survives to the ocean is a record of labour, not a list of addresses.
